name: Abul Hussain
seoTitle: Abul Hussain: Writer and Leader of Bengal's Freedom of Thought Movement
seoDescription: Abul Hussain was a Bengali writer, economist, and social activist who helped lead the Muslim Sahitya-Samaj and its freedom-of-thought movement in Dhaka.
contribution: Abul Hussain wrote essays and books on education, society, peasant life, and Muslim culture in Bengal. At the University of Dhaka, he became a leading force behind the Muslim Sahitya-Samaj, founded in 1926 to promote freedom of thought and modern literary debate. He also edited its periodical Shikha.
context: Dhaka's interwar intellectual world, where teachers and writers debated education, social reform, language, and the relationship between religious tradition and modern knowledge.
impact: His essays helped connect literary modernism with questions of education and social reform among Bengali Muslims. The Muslim Sahitya-Samaj and Shikha circle brought together writers including Kazi Abdul Wadud, Qazi Motahar Husain, Muhammad Shahidullah, and Abul Fazl, leaving a durable mark on twentieth-century Bengali intellectual history.
